u-dui-1-24in.summary: 1st Battalion, 24th Infantry Regiment, nicknamed "Deuce Four". The battalion was reactivated on 24 August 1995. Its Iraq-era Soldiers called themselves the "Punishers"; the skull marked "24" is their unofficial emblem. The regiment it carries on was organized in 1869 and had all-Black enlisted ranks (Buffalo Soldiers).
facts: Picture: an unofficial morale emblem (a skull marked "24") supplied by the app owner for the Punishers era. It is not an Army insignia and no Army record approves it.
Variant picture: the 24th Infantry Regiment's official distinctive unit insignia, a blockhouse on a blue disc with the scroll "San Juan".

Heritage: the regiment was organized 1 November 1869 from the 38th and 41st Infantry Regiments, with all-Black enlisted ranks. In 1898 it assaulted the Spanish blockhouse and trenches on San Juan Hill, Cuba.

1916: Mexican border, then General Pershing's Punitive Expedition. World War II: South Pacific from April 1942, including Guadalcanal. Korea: deployed June 1950 and earned the Republic of Korea Presidential Unit Citation for the Pusan defense. Inactivated 1 October 1951.
Battalion since 1995: reactivated 24 August 1995 in the 1st Brigade, 25th Infantry Division. Iraq 2007-08 (Diyala, Meritorious Unit Citation); Afghanistan 2011-12 (Zabul).
Deuce4.com, a veteran-led site that says it is not an official Army site, describes today's identity as the "Arctic Legion", with Soldiers serving in Alaska, and honors the Iraq-era "Punishers".
sources: Deuce4.com, "A Living Legacy" (https://deuce4.com/a-living-legacy/), a veteran-led initiative, not an official Army site
Skull picture: supplied by the app owner; unofficial, source of the artwork not confirmed
Regiment insignia picture: Wikimedia Commons, 24 Infantry Regiment DUI.png (public domain) - see CREDITS.md
